clue.text: Wife of a Trojan king, inspirational leader beheaded by his adopted country

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the leader's name is dropped

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary icon whose face adorns countless posters
Che, born in Argentina, made his name in Cuba

explanation.surface: A queen of Troy is linked to a revolutionary hero who loses his head in the land he adopted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspirational leader' is Che Guevara, Argentine-born but a hero of Cuba's revolution; 'beheaded' drops his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Hecuba was queen to Priam, ruler of Troy.

clue.text: Foreign gent greeting son up on pass

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy or son
to pass, as time does, is to go

explanation.surface: A foreign gentleman greets his son as he goes up a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAD into DAL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish nobleman of the lower ranks, so a gentleman from abroad.

clue.text: Currency that might introduce a list

definitions.meaning: the colón is the money of Costa Rica, formerly also of El Salvador
the punctuation mark of two dots often comes before a list of items

explanation.surface: A currency that might start off a list.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the Costa Rican money unit and the two-dot punctuation mark.

clue.text: Snake-like creature's undiscerning malignant software

parts.note: unable to see or discern, so blind
a worm is a self-spreading piece of malicious computer code

explanation.surface: A snake-like creature is described as a careless piece of malicious code.
explanation.definitionFit: The blindworm, or slowworm, is a legless lizard that looks like a small serpent.

clue.text: Competing boxer's seconds question almighty setback?

parts.note: how is a question word

indicators.note: set back means the word for the deity is written backwards

parts.note: the Almighty is God

explanation.surface: A boxer's corner men question whether the Almighty has dealt a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is a dog breed, not a fighter, which is why his 'seconds' mislead. 'setback' turns GOD into DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a breed of dog, and one entered in a competition is a show animal.

clue.text: A bit of rubbish Les cast outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside, wrapping the word for rubbish
cast in the sense of thrown about, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name, taken letter by letter
naff is British slang for tacky or rubbish

explanation.surface: Les throws a bit of rubbish outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges the name and 'outside' wraps it round British slang for poor quality. 'A bit' looks like 'a small piece' but is the horse's mouthpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A snaffle is a simple type of bit, the mouthpiece of a horse's bridle.

clue.text: Vigour of brass player's sound not top grade

indicators.note: A is the top grade, so the letter A is removed

parts.note: oompah is the rhythmic sound of a tuba or brass band

explanation.surface: A brass player's sound lacks the vigour to earn top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: Grade A is the top mark, so 'not top grade' drops the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for energy, zest or attractiveness.

clue.text: About to join Resistance? Respect!

indicators.note: the word for about joins the other word by entering it

parts.note: defence is resistance to attack
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to sign up for the Resistance and show it respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to join' slips the word for about into the word for resistance, after its fourth letter; the capital R makes 'Resistance' look like the wartime underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference is polite submission or respect towards another.

clue.text: Blow it, you must be mad!

definitions.text: Blow it, you must be mad!

parts.words: Blow it, you must be mad
parts.note: to blow a ... is the idiom for losing one's temper, so the item blown is a seal that marks someone as mad

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry telling someone they are crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mad here is angry: to blow a gasket is to lose one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasket is an engine seal, and the idiom about blowing one means flying into a rage.

clue.text: Person with craft to aggressively push drug

parts.note: to barge is to push roughly
E is the crossword abbreviation for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone skilled shoving drugs on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill but is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargee works a canal boat, so is a person in charge of a vessel.

clue.text: Exiled leader overturned by advanced African country and American son

indicators.note: overturned means the whole string that follows is read backwards

parts.note: Mali is in West Africa
a lad is a son

explanation.surface: An exiled leader is toppled by an African state and an American's son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned by' reverses AMALIALAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan Buddhist spiritual head has lived in exile in India since 1959.

clue.text: Winter wear makes a dog's dinner

definitions.meaning: warm tubes for the hands or ears worn in cold weather
botches or bungles; a dog's dinner is British slang for a mess

explanation.surface: Cold-weather clothing that turns things into a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear and hand warmers share their name with a verb meaning to fumble or bungle; a dog's dinner is British slang for a mess.

clue.text: Scored, though visibly ageing?

definitions.meaning: marked with lines, as scored paper is
a wrinkled face shows its years

explanation.surface: Marked with scratches, as though showing one's years.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled or scored paper and a wrinkled old face are both described by the same word for having lines.

clue.text: Freebie (oral examination not recommended)

parts.note: the proverb says never look a present animal in the mouth, which is the oral examination

explanation.surface: Something free, with a warning not to check it over by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'never look a gift horse in the mouth' warns against checking a present's teeth, as one would to age a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial present animal is any free gift that should be accepted without fault-finding.

clue.text: Performing with belt up on rock at the beach?

parts.note: a performer is on stage
belt up is British slang for be quiet, so sh
ore is rock containing metal

explanation.surface: A performer, told to shut up, sits on a rock by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on dry land at the coast, rather than at sea, is located by the shoreline.

clue.text: Salt distributor used as fire extinguisher?

definitions.meaning: a shaker that scatters salt over food
an overhead device that sprays water to put out fires

explanation.surface: A salt cellar pressed into service to put out a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a salt shaker and a ceiling fire-suppression device scatter drops or grains, so both share the name.

clue.text: Old Jewish sect lessened without its extreme elements

indicators.note: the extreme letters of the word are its ends, so the first and last are dropped

explanation.surface: An ancient sect, diminished, has lost its extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without its extreme elements' drops the L and D from LESSENED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish group around the time of Christ, linked to the Dead Sea Scrolls.

clue.text: Spanish town elevated since protecting translated almanac

indicators.note: the reversed letters go round the rearranged word, guarding it
in a down entry, raised means read upwards, so the word for since is reversed

parts.note: as means since, as in 'as it rained'

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A town raised high, since it guards a translated almanac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reverses the word for since in this down entry; 'protecting' splits its two letters round the anagram that 'translated' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamanca is a university city in western Spain.

clue.text: Cross borne by gutless chap holding back

indicators.note: the shortened word for chap holds the other inside it
losing the guts means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a guy is a chap
the rump is the back end

explanation.surface: A cross is carried by a cowardly man who hangs back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' removes the middle letter of the word for chap, and 'holding' puts the back end between what is left. 'Cross' looks like a noun but means bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross and the answer are both everyday synonyms for bad-tempered.

clue.text: House supporter one's gently touched, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that is spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: one is kissed, spoken as you're kissed

explanation.surface: A supporter of the House is said to be gently touched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' signals a soundalike: 'you're kissed' comes out close to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan of the House of York in the Wars of the Roses backed that royal dynasty.

clue.text: Canaries ocean formations

definitions.meaning: roller canaries are a breed of songbird known for their rolling song

explanation.surface: Canary Islands and the ocean's formations.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names a breed of trilling songbird and long breaking waves rolling in from the sea.

clue.text: Run with Brummie's stalked cluster of flowers

parts.note: a race is a run
Brummie is the setter, so the setter's word for himself

explanation.surface: A run with a Birmingham man's bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie, a word for someone from Birmingham, is the setter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a flower spike with blooms on short stalks along a central stem.

clue.text: Pierrot-like? Yes — dead sloppy!

indicators.note: sloppy means careless and messy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Is this sad clown deathly dull? Yes, dead sloppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloppy' rearranges YESDEAD. 'Dead' looks like slang for very.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot, the pantomime clown, wears a melancholy face with a painted tear.

clue.text: Having a gap year off, Kevin, say, died

indicators.note: Y is short for year, and off means it is removed

parts.note: Kevin Spacey, the actor

explanation.surface: A gap year off ends sadly with Kevin's death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a gap year' reads as one phrase but splits after 'gap'; 'year off' drops the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Things with gaps between them are set apart at intervals.

clue.text: Praise agency rip off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Praise for an agency is a rip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges AGENCYRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A panegyric is a formal speech or text of high praise.

clue.text: Must move with time: I appreciate that

parts.note: to go is to move
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A grateful acknowledgement that one has to keep up with the times.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal contraction of 'have got to' means the same as must.

clue.text: Contrary corporation has media chief silenced

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the word for corporation is reversed

parts.note: corporation is old jocular slang for a paunch, a tum
ED is an editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: An awkward company has silenced its head of media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' reverses TUM. Corporation is jocular slang for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted means quietened or made silent.

clue.text: Sound as a bell, having taken hard substance

indicators.note: the bell sound takes the letter for hard inside it

parts.note: ting is the sound a small bell makes
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: As sound as a bell, having taken some hard substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy; it is the noise. 'having taken' puts H inside TING.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an object or piece of matter, any substance in general.

clue.text: Body armour fashion around start of eighties

indicators.note: the word for fashion goes around the letter picked out

parts.note: a cult is a fad or fashion

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Body armour was the fashion at the start of the eighties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts E, from 'start of eighties', inside CULT.
explanation.definitionFit: A culet was a piece of plate armour guarding the lower back and hips.

clue.text: Setter's toilet has use of computers etc — yen for greatness!

parts.note: setter's is short for the setter is, so I'm
the men's is a gents' toilet
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: The setter's toilet has computers and a craving for grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like longing but is the Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Immensity is vastness, enormous size or greatness.

clue.text: "Resting" TV presenter's after reduced student accommodation

indicators.note: the presenter comes after the shortened accommodation
reduced means cut short, so the word for accommodation loses its ending

parts.note: a dormitory is a hall of residence
Ant McPartlin of the British TV double act Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A TV presenter is 'resting' after his student digs were cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant is half of Ant and Dec, a famous British TV presenting pair. 'Resting' in quotes is the actor's euphemism for out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or asleep, as a resting volcano or seed is.

clue.text: Posh car, say, reversing at end of road that's irregular?

parts.note: a Jag is a Jaguar, an upmarket car

indicators.note: reversing turns the abbreviation for say backwards

parts.note: eg means for example, as say does

indicators.note: the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A posh car reversing at the end of a road that's not straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns EG into GE; D is from 'at end of road'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with sharp, uneven points and edges is irregular in outline.
